children: , the global automaker and manufacturing group, put a huge number on its automation ambitions: roughly 1 trillion of potential annual spending beginning in 2028. U.S. shares slipped about 1.3% to $191.37, based on the latest price shown in the chart.

Toyota estimates that its factories, affiliates and major suppliers could ultimately require around 400,000 humanoid and conventional robots. The spending would go well beyond simply buying machines. It could also fund replacement of aging equipment, automated logistics and more human-machine collaboration across Toyota's manufacturing network. Management has not yet committed to the full program, however, and has not disclosed how many years the investment cycle could run.

The valuation picture adds another angle. At $191.37, Toyota trades about 8.04% below its GF Value estimate of $208.10, suggesting the market is still pricing the shares below GuruFocus' estimate of fair value. Mechanically spreading 1 trillion across 400,000 robots works out to roughly 2.5 million, or about $16,000, per machine, but that is not a true robot cost because the budget also includes systems, infrastructure and facility upgrades. The real investment case will come down to execution: how fast Toyota deploys the automation, how much labor and downtime it removes, and whether those productivity gains can justify the size of the spending program.

title: Toyota Drops as 400,000 Robots Meet a 1 Trillion Budget
